text:
maya: FYI team — product wants a new dashboard that ties runtime routing policy decisions to cost and latency. We need runtime and infra inputs: route decision counts, model_variant chosen, kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_size, and per-request token estimate. Can ops/infra agree on exporters and aggregation windows?
ryan: +1. From infra side I think we can add those tags to our runtime exporter. main questions: cardinality (model_variant + route + customer_id?) and retention.
sasha: We should definitely avoid customer_id at high cardinality. Recommend metric labels: model_variant, route_policy (e.g. low_latency, low_cost, fallback), region. No customer_id in raw metrics; use sampled logs for per-customer debugging.
tom: Agree on sampled traces for customer debugging. For dashboards we can support a per-route drilldown that hits traces, not raw metrics.
maya: Good call. For aggregation window: product wants near-real-time latency view (1m), but cost trends can be hourly. Proposal: exporter emits 1s counters + histograms, aggregation job rolls up to 1m and 1h buckets. Retention: 30d hot (1m/1h), 365d rolled-up (daily). Thoughts?
ryan: That sounds fine. Storage estimate: current token/metric volume suggests ~2.3TB/day additional when we keep 1m histograms for everything. We can reduce by pre-aggregating at exporter for common routes.
julie: Can we pre-aggregate at exporter for route_policy=low_cost only? That would cut volume. Also add sampling for model_variant where traffic < 0.5% to 1/100 sampling.
sasha: Sampling is okay but we need deterministic sampling for debugging (hash-based). Also expose sampled_count metric so dashboards can scale rates.
opentelemetry-bot: New metric schema proposal uploaded: /telemetry/schemas/runtime-routing-v1.yaml (see pasted below).
paula: Quick note: billing/finance will need a cost delta estimate for Dedicated customers if retention increases. Please cc finance@redwood on final plan.
ryan: Schema (short):

```
metrics:
  - name: redwood.runtime.route_decisions
    type: counter
    labels: [model_variant, route_policy, region]
  - name: redwood.runtime.kv_cache_hit_count
    type: counter
    labels: [model_variant, route_policy, region]
  - name: redwood.runtime.batch_size_hist
    type: histogram
    labels: [model_variant, route_policy]
  - name: redwood.runtime.sampled_token_estimate
    type: gauge
    labels: [model_variant]
```

ryan: Exporter config that we can push (example):

```
exporters:
  runtime:
    emit_intervals: 10s
    pre_aggregate:
      - labels: [route_policy, model_variant]
        rollup: true
    sampling:
      model_variant:
        threshold: 0.5
        sample_rate: 0.01
```

maya: Nice. A few operational asks: 1) add a metric redwood.runtime.exporter_error_count so we can monitor exporter health, 2) dashboard must show rollout flags (canary percentage) so product can correlate rollout -> latency spikes.
julie: We also need to decide backfill window. Product asked for 90-day historical comparison for cost/latency trends. Full backfill of all 90 days at 1m granularity is expensive. Proposal: backfill last 7 days at 1m, 30 days at 1h, 90 days at 1d. 
tom: +1 to tiered backfill. We'll run an offline aggregation job that consumes raw event logs. Job name suggestion: exporter-aggregate-backfill-2026-03. We can make it incremental to avoid cluster storms.
sasha: Also add a retention policy in the schema: hot_1m: 7d, hot_1h: 30d, cold_daily: 365d. Make it configurable per-tenant later.
ryan: Implementation constraints: aggregation workers need ~8 cores + 64GB each for peak backfill; estimate 12 workers for 30d->1h backfill of last month. Cost estimate ~USD 2.1k one-time cloud compute.
maya: OK. Prioritization: product wants initial dashboard in 2 sprints. Steps: 1) finalize schema + exporter change (ryan), 2) rollout exporter on canary infra (10% routes) (tom), 3) run backfill plan for last 30 days hourly (tom + infra), 4) dashboard UI and mapping of metrics to tiles (paula/product). Who wants to own the rollout doc?
julie: I can own the rollout doc and canary runbook. Will draft and share by EOD Friday.
ryan: I'll open a PR with the exporter changes and schema. Will tag @julie and @tom for rollout plan.
sasha: Small API debate: do we expose model_variant as a free string or enforced enum? Enums are better for aggregation but require model onboarding. Maybe start as free string but maintain a normalization map in the pipeline to avoid cardinality explosion.
maya: Let's normalize in the pipeline as sasha suggests. We'll maintain a map file and sync with model onboarding.
opentelemetry-bot: CI test for exporter changes: runtime-exporter/unit-tests passed.
tom: One more thing — dashboards should include a "fallback rate" derived metric: fallback_count / route_decisions. Add fallback_count to schema.
ryan: Added fallback_count in updated schema. Pushing PR now.
paula: I'll loop in finance and product. Also suggest we add a quick cost gauge tile to the dashboard (USD/day est) so PMs can see delta.
maya: Great. Action items summary:
- ryan: PR for exporter + schema.
- tom: canary rollout on 10% routes + infra backfill job.
- julie: rollout doc + runbook.
- sasha: normalization map and sampling rules.
- paula: product + finance comms + dashboard tile spec.
Everyone: please react with :thumbsup: if you agree or drop concerns here.
ryan: :thumbsup:
julie: :thumbsup:
sasha: :thumbsup:
tom: :thumbsup:
paula: :thumbsup:
maya: Thanks all — I'll track this in the eng-platform board and add the tickets. If anything urgent, ping me in #eng-oncall.
